articles.headline: The Book Depository of the African M.E. Church (standing ad) -- address now No. 631 Pine
articles.summary: The Book Depository of the African M.E. Church, No. 631 Pine Street, Philadelphia. Keeps on hand, in connexion with other books, Sabbath School books of various kinds, Question Books, Catechisms Nos. 1, 2 and 3, books generally used in the Public Schools, also stationery, inks, pens, envelopes and blank books. CHANGED: the standing Book Depository ad now prints No. 631 Pine (the General Book Steward's office moved there Nov. 1866); the ad had still read 619 Pine through the spring quarter, so the address is newly updated.

articles.headline: Liberty Hall (notice)
articles.summary: Liberty Hall -- one of the finest halls in the city, situated on Lombard street below 8th, having two large stores on the first floor, two fine basement stores, and a large auditorium on the second floor, 40 by 80 feet, in which lectures, concerts, and fairs are held. Application for the use of the hall may be made to Rev. S. Smith, 921 Lombard street. Dated June 28th.
people: agent for use of Liberty Hall (Rev.), 921 Lombard street [initial uncertain, S or J]

articles.headline: Notice (wife desertion)
articles.author: J. W. H. Cathcart
articles.summary: Whereas, my wife, Sarah Cathcart, has voluntarily left my bed and board, all persons are hereby forbid harboring or trusting her on my account, as I will pay no debts of her contracting from this date, July 2d, 1867. J. W. H. Cathcart, No. 210 Quince St.

articles.headline: Died (Jacob Hunter; Mary Elizabeth Shelton)
articles.summary: On the 12th of June, Jacob Hunter, late Steward of Lincoln University [Chester County, Pa.], aged 78 years. He was born in the State of Maryland, but removed to Chester County, Pa., when 18 years old, where he became a member of the Fagg's Manor Presbyterian Church the same year; a pious, industrious man, leaving a widow and several children. On the 23d of June, at 8 o'clock, Mary Elizabeth, daughter of Harriet and Isaac Shelton, aged one year and six months (place not stated).
people: deceased; late steward of Lincoln University, aged 78

articles.headline: Married (Barrett-Reddin)
articles.summary: On the 18th of July, Mr. Joseph Barrett, of Dover, Del., to Miss Rachel Reddin, of Chester City, Pa., by Rev. Wm. Murphy.

articles.headline: Obituaries (Lydia Lane; Wm. Reeves)
articles.summary: Departed this life June 20, 1867, in the triumphs of faith, Sister Lydia Lane, in her 9[5]th year, at Brooklyn, Ill., mother of the well-known Sister Priscilla of Baltimore (signed W. R. R., St. Louis, July 18 -- non-Philadelphia). July 17th, 1867, in the hope of a blissful immortality, Wm. Reeves, aged 16 years (no place of death stated).
people: deceased, aged 16 (place of death not stated)

articles.headline: Notice ('Shall I Call?') -- minister returning North, Philadelphia address 1081 Warnock St
articles.author: R. P. [surname uncertain]
articles.summary: A minister writing from Savannah, Ga. (July 18), intends to return North in a few days and to visit his brother ministers and assist their meetings, asking that replies be sent to him at 1081 Warnock street, Philadelphia (he leaves the South July 27th). He reports that the people in Savannah, under the management of Rev. Anthony L. Stanford, have begun erecting a new church but have not been able to complete it, and references letters from Rev. R. H. Cain of Charleston, S.C., and Rev. T. G. Steward. Signed R. P. [G---].
people: managing the erection of a new church at Savannah (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Cape May
articles.author: Wm. Whipper
articles.summary: A letter from Cape May on the summer season at the resort: large delegations present from Washington, Baltimore, Philadelphia and elsewhere, and a brilliant and successful lecture by Miss Fanny H. Jackson on the popular subject of 'Suffrage,' warmly received. The writer closes with reflections on distinguished colored representatives -- in literature and science a Wheatley, a Fuller and a Banneker (Maryland); in theology a Coker, a Pennington and a Douglass; in oratory a Douglass, a Ward, a Garnet and a Harper -- and names Fanny M. Jackson as the District of Columbia's distinguished representative in science and oratory. Signed Wm. Whipper. (Fanny H./M. Jackson = Fanny Jackson, principal of the Institute for Colored Youth; Wm. Whipper = the abolitionist and lumber merchant.)
people: delivered a lecture on 'Suffrage' at Cape May (Miss; = Fanny M. Jackson, principal of the Institute for Colored Youth)

events.name: Book Committee (Committee on Aid for the Book Concern) -- report and division of the $7000 debt
events.location: Philadelphia (A.M.E. Book Concern)
events.description: The Book Committee, having charge of the affairs of the Book Concern in the interval of the General Conference, met July 1, 1867, and recommended raising $7000 to liquidate the present indebtedness of the Book Concern, the Philadelphia Conference having jurisdiction over the Concern during the interval. The whole amount was divided among the districts: Baltimore $1000, Philadelphia $1000, New York $700, New England $800, Ohio $1000, Indiana $700, Missouri $550, Louisiana $350, S. Carolina $550, Georgia $200, Virginia $150, Alabama $125, California $200 (several amounts uncertain on film). Reported 'By order of the Conference.' The accompanying editorial (p.2, 'Let every preacher in the A.M.E. Church read this again and again') appealed to the District Book Stewards -- W. R. Revels (Missouri), W. C. Trevan (Indiana), John Turner (Ohio), Henry Davis (New York), H. M. Turner (Georgia), T. M. D. Ward (California), G. T. Watkins (Virginia), all outside the Philadelphia Conference. Committee member N. H. Turpin is of the New York Conference (Bridge St., Brooklyn) and is left in the text only.
attendees: chairman (Rev.; General Book Steward and Editor)
secretary (Rev.; late editor of the Recorder)

events.name: Appointments of the New York Conference -- transfers into the Philadelphia Conference
events.location: Philadelphia Conference
events.description: The printed appointments of the New York Annual Conference closed with several transfers: D. Darroll transferred to the Philadelphia Conference and appointed to Bethel church, Phila.; J. S. Leuken transferred to the Philadelphia Conference and appointed to Egg Harbour, N.J.; James M. Williams transferred to the Philadelphia Conference and appointed to Trenton, N.J. (Also, outside the Philadelphia Conference: Alex Posey transferred to the Baltimore Conference, appointed to Frederick City, Md.; and Syren Buey transferred to the South Carolina Conference.) Several surnames uncertain on microfilm.
attendees: transferred to Philadelphia Conference, appointed to Trenton, N.J.

events.name: First Quarterly Meeting, A.M.E. Wesley church, Hurst St. (Little Wesley), Philadelphia
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley church, Hurst St., Philadelphia
events.description: Notice (headed 'NOTICE, EVERYBODY!'): the first Quarterly Meeting of the A.M.E. Wesley church, Hurst St., Philadelphia, to take place July 14th; love feast in the morning, doors open at 8 o'clock. Signed by the pastor, whose name on film reads G. E. B[u/a]xer (surname illegible/uncertain -- left out of linked names). Hurst St Wesley = Little Wesley (A.M.E.), per owner's ruling.

events.name: Quarterly Meeting, Oxford St. Church, Frankford, Philadelphia
events.location: Oxford St. Church, Frankford, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the Quarterly Meeting of the Oxford St. Church, Frankford, Philadelphia, to take place Sunday July 14th, at which time the Revs. Wm. Moore, E. Weaver and others will be present. Come one, come all, to the help of the Lord against the mighty. Signed D. P. Seaton, Pastor.

events.name: Quarterly meetings, West Philadelphia Circuit (Norristown, West Philadelphia, Germantown)
events.location: West Philadelphia Circuit (Norristown; West Philadelphia; Germantown, Pa.)
events.description: Notice of quarterly meetings of the West Philadelphia Circuit: Norristown, Sunday July 14th; West Philadelphia, Sunday July 21st; Germantown, Pa., Sunday July 28th, 1867; Quarterly Conference at West Philadelphia on Saturday evening July 20th at 8 o'clock. H. J. Rhodes, Minister in charge.
attendees: minister in charge (Rev.), West Philadelphia Circuit

events.name: Quarterly meetings, Burlington Circuit (Burlington, Mount Holly, Evesham, N.J.)
events.location: Burlington Circuit, N.J. (Philadelphia Conference)
events.description: Notice of quarterly meetings of the Burlington Circuit: Burlington, July 14th; Mount Holly, July 20th (Quarterly Conference at 10 o'clock a.m.) and Quarterly meeting Sabbath, July 21st; Evesham, July 28th, 1867. J. M. Mitchell, Pastor.

events.name: Quarterly meetings, Penningtonville Circuit (Chester Co., Pa.)
events.location: Penningtonville Circuit, Chester County, Pa.
events.description: Notice of quarterly meetings of the Penningtonville Circuit: Welch Mountain, July 7th; Black Rock, July 14th; Midway, July 21st; Penningtonville, July 28th, 1867. William H. Turner, Preacher in charge.

events.name: Union A.M.E. church (Coates St) -- new organ opening
events.location: Union A.M.E. church, Coates Street below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the members of the Union A.M.E. church, Coates Street below Fifth, under the pastoral care of Rev. Wm. Moore, have recently secured by purchase a very superior organ, built by Mr. J. Hayes Carter. The opening will take place on Thursday evening next, July 11th. The organs built by Mr. Carter have merited the choicest commendations of the public. (J. Hayes Carter = Joseph H. Carter, the Black organ builder of South Street, per owner's ruling.)

events.name: Bethany Mission Temperance Association -- first regular meeting
events.location: Mission House, Brandywine Street above 15th, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the first regular meeting of the 'Bethany Mission Temperance Association' to be held Monday evening, July 8th, at 8 o'clock, in the Mission House, Brandywine Street, above 15th. Young men generally invited to attend, and to join the Society. (Street reads 'Bromly wine Street' on film = Brandywine Street.)

events.name: Union Grand Tabernacle No. 1 (Grand United Order) -- yearly meeting, election and installation of officers
events.location: Hall rear of A.M.E. Macedonia church, Spruce Street, South Camden, N.J.
events.description: The yearly meeting of the Union Grand Tabernacle, No. 1, was held at their hall, rear of the A.M.E. Macedonia church, Spruce Street, South Camden, on the third Wednesday, June 19th, 1867. The following named persons were duly elected and installed: Isaiah Swayne, G.O. Sent.; Lydia Hamilton, G.I. Sent.; Lucinda Gordan, G.W. Cond.; Tracey A. Julius, G.A. Cond.; Elizabeth Christopher, G.H.S.; Elizabeth Parker, G.D.W.V.S.; Jas. Williams, G.D.W.S.; Hannah Emery, G.W.V.S.; John H. Bean, G.W.S. Persons wishing to be formed into tabernacles can do so by addressing Jas. E. Simpson, R.C.S., Spruce St., South Camden, N.J. Attest: A. B. White, G. Scribe; Josiah Cornelius, R.G.D.M.
attendees: R.C.S. (contact for new tabernacles), Spruce St., South Camden

events.name: Philadelphia Conference camp meeting announced
events.location: Media, Pa.
events.description: Editorial notice: the brethren of the Philadelphia Conference have decided to hold a camp meeting at Media, Pa., to commence on the 2?th of August (digit uncertain on film; read as 24th), intending that it not be conducted as small 'mock' meetings have been heretofore; it is to take place soon after Bishop Campbell's Conference and camp meeting are over.

events.name: Rev. Deaton Dorrell enters on his duties as pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.location: Bethel Church (Mother Bethel A.M.E.), Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial ('Rev. Deaton Dorrell and the Bethel Church, Philadelphia'): Brother Dorrell, transferred from the New York Conference to the charge of Bethel Church, arrived in the city on last Friday [July 5] and entered upon his duties at Bethel on Sabbath morning, taking his text from John xiv. 15 ('If ye love me, keep my commandments'); the occasion was the administration of the Lord's Supper, the discourse practical, plain and pleasing, and the editor was pleased that he commenced at 10 o'clock and held the service but one hour. Name printed 'Deaton Dorrell' in the heading, 'Denton Dorrell' in the contents, and 'D. Darroll' in the July 6 New York Conference appointments; he remitted subscriptions from Brooklyn, N.Y. as 'Rev. D. Dorrell.'
attendees: pastor (Rev.) of Bethel Church, Philadelphia [first name Deaton/Denton uncertain]

events.name: Fourth of July observances in Philadelphia -- Liberty Hall meeting and Independence Square temperance meeting
events.location: Liberty Hall (Lombard St below 8th) and Independence Square, Philadelphia
events.description: The Fourth of July passed off quietly in the city. A temperance meeting was held in Independence Square, and a meeting of colored people in Liberty Hall. D. B. Bowers presided over the Liberty Hall meeting; Secretaries were appointed; the meeting was opened by Mr. Harman; addresses were made by Professor [Green?] and Rev. William Moore; the well-known Hannibal Cornet Band was present and discoursed excellent music. (D. B. Bowers = D. B. Bowser, the Philadelphia artist, per owner's record.)
attendees: president of the Liberty Hall Fourth of July meeting

events.name: Fourth of July temperance celebration, Mount Holly / Clarksboro, N.J.
events.location: Mount Holly and Clarksboro, N.J. (Burlington Circuit, Philadelphia Conference)
events.description: Letter from Mt. Holly, N.J. (dated July 6): the Fourth of July was celebrated in fine style. A celebration was held at the Court House, and a temperance pic-nic in a grove near Mt. Holly; a band from Philadelphia furnished music and distinguished vocalists sang. Temperance addresses were made by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell and Rev. Theo. Gould. In the evening a festival was held in the school-house at Clarksboro, and a lecture was delivered in the A.M.E. Church, of which Rev. Mr. Mitchell is pastor.
attendees: speaker (Rev.); pastor of the Clarksboro A.M.E. Church

events.name: Acknowledgment -- First Colored Church (Rev. Theodore D. Miller), Philadelphia: contributors to the first payment on the new church
events.location: First Colored Church (Rev. Theodore D. Miller, pastor), formerly of Eleventh and Pearl Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Acknowledgment of money received during the first struggle to raise $10,000, the first payment having been made within seventy days of the contract for the First Colored Church, formerly of Eleventh and Pearl Streets, Phila., Rev. Theodore D. Miller, pastor. $21 was raised by Mr. George Gray; the whole amount received and paid over was about $55. Contributors as printed (with amounts): Mrs. Sarah Young $1; Rev. J. Frisby $2.50; Mrs. Mary Brown $1; Rev. Wm. Winder; Rev. E. Weaver $1; Rev. R. P. Gibbs $1; Rev. Wm. H. Davy $1; Rev. John Peterson $1; Rev. J. B. Revel $1; Rev. R. P. Seaton; Rev. Frisby J. Cooper $1; Jeremiah Young $1; Mrs. C. Gilbert $1; Mrs. Sarah A. Jordan $1; Miss Adeline Smith; Mr. Abraham Fields $1; Moses Anderson $1; Mrs. J. C. White $1; Mrs. C. Jackson $1; Mr. Morris $5; Dr. J. G. Allen $5; Mr. George Gray $5; Mr. Henry Cropper; Mrs. Button $1; James H. Lewis $1; John R. Porter $1; Wm. C. Curtis $1; Henry Chatham $1; John A. Warren $1; Jenny M. Davis $1; John T. Brown $1; George Costin $1; Georgianna Sawyer $1; Mrs. H. Duterte $2; Lewis K. Seymour $1; E. V. C. Bain $2; M. B. Cost $1; Mrs. H. Ferman $1; J. P. Kidd $1. Signed A. M. Cropper, July 20, 1867. (Rev. E. Weaver = Elisha Weaver; Mrs. H. Duterte = Henrietta Duterte; Abraham Fields = the grocer; Rev. Theodore D. Miller = Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, whose 'Masonry and Christianity' sermon was sold at 508 Quince St.)

events.name: Festival/surprise for the minister of an A.M.E. Church ('Well Done') -- locality not legible
events.location: A.M.E. Church, locality not read (dateline illegible; out-of-town correspondence)
events.description: 'Well Done' correspondence: the ladies of the place surprised the minister of the A.M.E. Church by decorating the chapel (within about eight hours) and providing a feast of berries, cake, cream, lemonade, ice water, etc. The ladies named: Mrs. Mary A. Cole, Mrs. Frank Johnson, Mrs. Fanny Jackson, Mrs. Selina Grayson, Miss Williams, Miss Dukes, and George Simmons, Esq. Net proceeds $96.50, handed over by Mrs. Betsy Rolfe. Signed 'P.' The dateline place name is illegible on film, so this cannot be confirmed as Philadelphia; names are left in the description, not linked.

events.name: Quarterly meeting, Union A.M.E. church, Coates Street, Philadelphia
events.location: Union A.M.E. church, Coates Street below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: quarterly meeting at Union A.M.E. church, Coates Street below Fifth, Sunday July 21st. Preaching at 10 o'clock a.m. by Rev. James Hollen; at 3 o'clock p.m. by Rev. D. P. Seaton; and at 8 o'clock by Rev. J. B. Hamilton. Love Feast, Monday evening, 8 o'clock. Wm. Moore, Pastor. (James Hollen = the former Bethel pastor; D. P. Seaton also pastor of the Oxford St. Church, Frankford.)

events.name: Camp meeting at Evesham, N.J. (Rev. Jacob Mitchell)
events.location: Evesham, N.J.
events.description: Notice: Rev. Jacob Mitchell to hold a camp meeting at Evesham, N.J., commencing August 15th, to be conducted in the best order; no intoxicating liquor sold within two and a half miles of the ground; the stages to go from Market St. wharf (Philadelphia); fare 75 cents. Rev. Bishop Wayman to be present, with some of the best divines in the district -- Rev. W. Moore of Philadelphia, Rev. W. W. Grimes of New Jersey, Rev. W. H. Chase of Delaware, Rev. J. Woodlin of Brooklyn, and others. Applications for tents to the trustees. Jacob Mitchell, Preacher in charge.
attendees: to be present (Rev.), of New Jersey

events.name: D.G. Lodge No. 2 (Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria) -- officers elected
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: The following persons were elected officers of the D.G. Lodge, No. 2, of G.S. and D. of S. (Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria), on June 4, 1867: Henry H. Gilbert, W.G. Chief (residence No. 17[8] Addison St.); Ann Posey, W.G.P.D.; John Stevenson, G.D. Chief; Cornelia E. Gilbert, G.D. Daughter; Samuel Rivers, W.V. Chief; Sarah Newman, W.D. of Count; John Conmy, W.R.S.; Harriet Robinson, D. of R.; Daniel L. Thomas, F.S.; Alice Clark, F.D.; Stephen Smith, Treasurer; Elizabeth Martin, D. of T.; James Goldsborough, Prelate; Maria Highgates, D. of L.; John H. Bell, Conductor; Mary Branch, D. Conductress; Morris Maxwell, O.S.; Mary Sipple, D. of P.; George Whipper, S.S.; Ann Kinkade, D. of K.; Chauncey Leonard, G. Orator. (Maria Highgates = the shrouding woman of 1026 Barley.)
attendees: W.G. Chief, residence No. 17[8] Addison St.

events.name: Colored camp meeting at Elwood Grove, Westdale Station, Delaware County, Pa.
events.location: Elwood Grove, Westdale Station (West Chester Railroad), Delaware County, Pa.
events.description: Notice: a colored camp meeting to be held at Elwood Grove, Westdale Station, on the West Chester Railroad, Delaware county, commencing Thursday evening, August 1st, 1867. Excellent accommodations; the grove held under strict discipline; preaching on a large covered platform; a number of eminent preachers to officiate; the grove brilliantly illuminated each evening until 10 o'clock with large locomotive reflectors; excursion tickets sold on Sunday by the West Chester R.R. Co. to Westdale Station. Rev. Robert J. White, Superintendent.

events.name: Grand Union Camp Meeting for the State of Delaware (Mr. Ripple's Woods, near Fulton Station)
events.location: Mr. Ripple's Woods, about 1.5 miles from Fulton Station, Delaware
events.description: Notice: a grand Union Camp Meeting for the State of Delaware to be held in Mr. Ripple's Woods, about 1.5 miles from Fulton Station, to commence August 8th and continue to the 14th; persons from Philadelphia, Wilmington and other places can take the Delaware train and get off at Fulton Station. Signed H. H. Lewis; G. T. Waters; W. H. Chase, Pastor. (A Delaware camp meeting, accessible from Philadelphia; W. H. Chase of Delaware appears also in the Evesham, N.J. camp-meeting notice.)

events.name: Corner-stone laying, A.M.E. Church, Fortieth above Locust, West Philadelphia
events.location: A.M.E. Church, Fortieth street above Locust, West Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the corner-stone of the A.M.E. Church, Fortieth above Locust street, West Philadelphia, Pa., to be laid Thursday, August 1st, 1867 (weather permitting); ceremonies to commence at 2 o'clock P.M.; the presence of Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman and other distinguished divines expected; a collection to be raised for the church after the services. H. J. Rhodes, Minister-in-charge. (H. J. Rhodes is also minister in charge of the West Philadelphia Circuit.)
attendees: Bishop (Rev.; A. W. Wayman), expected to be present

events.name: Quarterly meeting, Bethel Church (Sixth above Lombard), Philadelphia
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth street above Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: a quarterly meeting at Bethel Church, Sixth street above Lombard, Sunday July 28. Preaching at 10 o'clock; at 3 o'clock by Rev. William Moore; at 8 by Rev. Jonathan Hamilton. Love Feast Monday evening at 8 o'clock. D. Dorrell, Pastor. (Bethel now pastored by Rev. Deaton/D. Dorrell.)

events.name: Frankford church (Oxford St) to be rebuilt under Rev. Seaton
events.location: Frankford Circuit (Oxford St. Church), Frankford, Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial 'Rev. Mr. Seaton and the Frankford Church': the young brother appointed to the Frankford Circuit at the last Conference is pushing his work along nicely; he and his congregation have decided to pull down their present old church and build up a new one, and Seaton has already raised a good sum. (Rev. Mr. Seaton = D. P. Seaton, pastor of the Oxford St. Church, Frankford, per the July 6 quarterly-meeting notice.)
attendees: pastor (Rev.), Frankford Circuit / Oxford St. Church

CR_1867-08-03 page 2 editorial/local notes: 'Quarterly Meeting' -- the editor reports a district quarterly meeting held last Sabbath (brief, no roster). A Delaware-river wharf (about 250 feet) gave way, engulfing persons standing on it and precipitating about 100 hogsheads of sugar into the river (Philadelphia local news, no named victims). 'Things in Philadelphia' -- the city authorities passed an ordinance forbidding all drinking saloons on the Sabbath. NOTICE 'Camp Meetings and Quarterly Meetings in the Suburbs of Philadelphia' -- an editorial noting the proliferation of camp meetings; the members of the Philadelphia Conference at their last sitting resolved to hold a grand Union Camp Meeting on AUGUST 28th (this is the Media, Pa. Philadelphia Conference camp meeting announced July 13 -- the commencement date, uncertain on July 13, is here given as the 28th), and Brother Mitchell and others contemplate a series of old-fashioned camp meetings. A Book Committee meeting notice (to meet at the Book store). 'Personal' -- Rev. R. [P.] Gibbs of the Savannah Station was seen. A camp-meeting editorial signed T. Gould (Rev. Theodore Gould). 'Cheering News from the Brethren' -- letters from Levi Keane (Indianapolis), Brother Evans (an Indianapolis corner-stone laying attended by Revs. Graham and Henry J. Young of the Indiana Conference), Brother Lewis (Washington Mission), and a Danville, Ky. correspondent -- all non-Phila. 'Letter from Bro. Wilkerson' = John M. Wilkinson, St. Joseph, Mo. (non-Phila). Repeats: the Book Concern report, the Liberty Hall notice, the Banneker House (Cape Island) notice.
